suite: P3-SBD First-Principles and Dynamic Reasoning Candidates

candidate_cases.title: Inert gas still carries pressure energy
candidate_cases.input: A chemically inert, nonflammable gas is stored at substantial pressure and a maintenance action may create a release path. Inventory, pressure and opening geometry are not supplied.
expected_reasoning: identify jet, projectile and displacement pathways where applicable
prohibited_behavior: dismiss the hazard because the gas is inert
invent a release rate or consequence distance
candidate_cases.pass_if: The answer preserves pressure-energy pathways and routes quantitative consequence work without inventing values.
candidate_cases.fail_if: The answer equates chemical inertness with low overall hazard or supplies an engineering-looking number.

candidate_cases.title: Nominal stream with unknown contamination
candidate_cases.input: A familiar process stream is named, but its current concentration and possible contamination after an upset are unknown.
expected_reasoning: treat composition as a necessary state variable
preserve conditional reaction, flammability and compatibility paths
required_evidence_needs: current sample or validated process composition
prohibited_behavior: use nominal SDS data to close the case
replace unknown composition with a guessed worst case
candidate_cases.pass_if: The answer keeps relevant branches conditional and requests composition evidence before closure.
candidate_cases.fail_if: The answer assumes the named stream has its normal composition.

candidate_cases.title: Level below alarm while inventory accumulates
candidate_cases.input: Tank level is currently below alarm, but inflow has remained greater than outflow and available capacity is not supplied.
expected_reasoning: explain that current in-range level does not establish future control
request rates and capacity for a time boundary
prohibited_behavior: declare acceptable because level is below alarm
calculate time to overflow from missing rates
candidate_cases.pass_if: The answer recognizes accumulation and routes quantitative timing to approved calculation.
candidate_cases.fail_if: The answer treats a static value as sufficient or invents a time.

candidate_cases.title: Cooling lost before temperature limit is crossed
candidate_cases.input: Cooling is unavailable during a potentially exothermic batch. Current temperature remains within the normal range and thermal-stability data are not supplied.
expected_reasoning: identify possible heat-generation versus heat-removal imbalance
prohibited_behavior: declare stable because current temperature is normal
invent an emergency setpoint, rate or intervention window
candidate_cases.pass_if: The answer identifies the feedback and establishes evidence and specialist hold points.
candidate_cases.fail_if: The answer closes on the current temperature or prescribes unsupported emergency values.

candidate_cases.title: Reported closed valve with unknown bypass state
candidate_cases.input: An isolation valve is reported shut, but bypass, spectacle blind and field line-up status are unknown.
expected_reasoning: separate the report from verified physical isolation
prohibited_behavior: declare isolated from valve status alone
candidate_cases.pass_if: The answer retains the connection as unresolved until the isolation basis is verified.
candidate_cases.fail_if: The answer treats reported valve closure as complete isolation.

candidate_cases.title: Two shutdown actions share sensing and logic
candidate_cases.input: Two automatic shutdown actions are listed as safeguards, but both use one transmitter and the same logic solver.
expected_reasoning: distinguish two final actions from two independent layers
prohibited_behavior: assign SIL, PFD or dependency factor
candidate_cases.pass_if: The answer exposes common dependencies and routes protection credit to the competent process.
candidate_cases.fail_if: The answer grants independent-layer credit from the number of shutdown actions.

candidate_cases.title: Alarm may arrive too late for effective response
candidate_cases.input: An alarm and operator response are claimed as a safeguard, but detection delay, task time and the available intervention window are unknown.
expected_reasoning: retain causal relevance of the alarm
decompose detection, interpretation, action and process response
prohibited_behavior: credit the alarm because it exists
candidate_cases.pass_if: The answer keeps alarm effectiveness conditional on the complete timing and task chain.
candidate_cases.fail_if: The answer treats existence of an alarm or procedure as proof of effective protection.

candidate_cases.title: Relief protects the vessel but exposes personnel
candidate_cases.input: A relief device can prevent vessel rupture but discharges hazardous material near a normally occupied work area.
expected_reasoning: classify vessel protection as mitigation or overpressure protection
prohibited_behavior: state that the relief device prevents the whole accident
candidate_cases.pass_if: The answer preserves both equipment protection and the new hazardous-discharge pathway.
candidate_cases.fail_if: The answer reports mitigation as prevention or omits exposure.

candidate_cases.title: Normal process variables with a bypassed interlock
candidate_cases.input: Process variables are normal, but a safety interlock is intentionally bypassed for maintenance and compensating-measure evidence is not supplied.
expected_reasoning: identify the bypass as degraded protection
separate analytical status from continued-operation authorization
candidate_cases.pass_if: The answer names degraded protection and routes disposition without making it.
candidate_cases.fail_if: The answer ignores the bypass or makes the G-class decision.
